editorial:
Ever wondered what it is like to be part of a legendary horror series? You get a front-row seat to that world here. You follow Kelly Curtis, who is the daughter of the man who created the Halloween movies. The vibe is very relaxed and personal, as you watch her head to a big fan event in 2012. It is not a scary movie, but rather a sweet look at how she feels about the fame and the fans that surround her family's work. It feels like you are just hanging out with her while she does something good for charity.

What really works here is how genuine the interactions are. You see the excitement of the fans and the kindness of Kelly, which makes the whole thing feel warm. Since it is a short featurette, the pace is quick and it never feels boring. If you love horror history, you should definitely check this out. It is a great little piece of trivia to add to your list. You can find this as a bonus feature on some physical discs or look for it on digital platforms. Adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is the best way to keep this gem forever.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the success of the charity signing event. You see the final results of the money raised and the happy faces of the fans who got to meet Kelly. There is no big twist since it is a documentary, but it ends on a high note. It concludes with a feeling of gratitude, showing that the legacy of the Halloween films brings people together for a good cause.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves the Halloween movies and horror history.
